h1: Window assembly machines — corner crimper, screwing and sash assembly, portable machines and conveyors
intro: Once the profiles are cut and machined, the frames are put together: aluminum corners are crimped over cleats, reinforcements and hardware are screwed in, and the sashes are fitted with their hardware. NovoTech supplies the machines for that from Plastmak, built in Bursa, Turkey: the SÇ 902 hydraulic corner crimper with 4 + 4 knives; single and double-head pneumatic screwing machines and a sash assembly machine that fits a double-opening sash's hardware in 3.5 minutes; the SÇ 221 and SÇ 551 portable notching and copy milling machines; and the SÇ 1000 digital measuring conveyor with the SÇ 1001 – 1003 conveyors that carry profiles to and from every machine. Supplied with a CSA-approved panel, installed and supported from Mississauga, ON, Canada.

faq.q: How is an aluminum frame joined?
faq.a: Aluminum profiles are not welded: a cleat (corner bracket) is pushed into the mitred ends, and the crimper drives knives into the profile walls over the cleat so they lock onto it. The SÇ 902 does it hydraulically with four knives a side, set to the profile with millimetre scales, while a pneumatic miter wedge holds the corner square.

faq.q: What does the sash assembly machine do?
faq.a: It fits the hardware of single and double-opening sashes without moulds or templates: it measures the sash, drills with a three-arm unit, mills the espagnolette groove and screws the hardware in, aligned by laser — 3.5 minutes on average for a double-opening window.

It sets the saw's length stop for you: type the length on the SÇ 1000's touch screen and the stop moves there to ±.020″ (±0.5 mm), then retracts at one push so the cut piece comes out. No tape and no reading errors, and it fits any of the saws.

faq.q: What voltage do these machines run on?
faq.a: Three-phase machines are supplied for 600 V as standard with a CSA-approved panel; 208 V, 240 V and 480 V 3-phase are available on request, and 240 V single-phase on models whose main motor is 2.2 kW (3 HP) or less — a machine with a motor above 2.2 kW must run on three-phase power and cannot be converted to 240 V single-phase. Manual machines have no electrics.
